questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The most crucial aspects when choosing my exchange destination were the opportunity to improve my French, living in a large and vibrant city, and experiencing everyday life in one place over a longer period. Paris offered a unique combination of culture, beauty, social life, and familiarity, while still being relatively close to home.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: While the academic and administrative aspects of the exchange did not always meet my expectations, the overall experience of living in Paris was incredibly rewarding. I met amazing people from all over the world, improved my French, and had the opportunity to experience one of the world's most vibrant cities from the perspective of a local rather than a tourist. Despite some challenges, I would still highly recommend the experience.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy to find the information I needed upon arrival. The information provided by the university was clear and helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The host university has an office for exchange students that is open most of the time. The staff were very helpful, welcoming, and patient, and they were always available to answer questions and assist with practical matters.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The assistance available upon arrival was very good. The staff at the international office were welcoming, patient, and always willing to help with practical questions. While some administrative processes could be confusing before arrival, I found the support on campus to be helpful and reassuring.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Finding off-campus housing was quite difficult and expensive. However, I found a room at Cité Universitaire in Paris, which is a unique accommodation option for international students. It is relatively affordable, located in beautiful surroundings, and offers everything a student might need, including study spaces, sports facilities, an inexpensive cafeteria, and a large international student community. I would highly recommend it to future exchange students.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Finding accommodation can be challenging, even if you start your search well in advance. I would strongly recommend looking into student residences as early as possible.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Finding housing was difficult and often expensive. While there are good accommodation options for students, securing a place can be a stressful process and requires planning well in advance.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not fully explore all the registration resources available at the host institution. Therefore, my rating reflects my personal experience, and other students may find the process easier if they make greater use of the available support.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process was quite unstructured. It was often unclear which courses were actually available, and I never received a complete overview of the course offerings before registration. Information about courses was frequently incomplete, and some registration links did not work properly. Registration deadlines were also postponed several times due to technical issues. As a result, the process felt somewhat confusing and unpredictable.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: An email support service was available, but response times were often very slow. In some cases, it was difficult to get a response at all, which made resolving issues challenging.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: In the end, I was able to register for the classes I wanted. Although the process initially felt quite frustrating and sometimes hopeless due to the lack of information and technical issues, the staff were very helpful once I arrived on campus. They were flexible and supportive in helping students adjust their schedules and resolve registration problems.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: My advice would be to be patient. The registration process can seem confusing and frustrating at times, but things usually work out in the end. Once you arrive, the staff are generally very helpful and willing to assist with any issues.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The academic programme offered some interesting and unique courses, and I particularly enjoyed subjects that were not available at my home institution. However, I generally found the academic level and workload to be lower than what I am used to at UCPH. The programme was valuable from an international and personal perspective, but academically it did not fully meet my expectations.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses covered interesting topics and I enjoyed several of them. However, I found the academic level to be somewhat lower than what I am used to at my home university, and the workload was generally less demanding.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style was quite different from UCPH. Most learning took place through classroom teaching, with less emphasis on independent study and academic reading. Compared to UCPH, the courses felt less academically demanding and more similar to a high school learning environment. There were relatively few required readings, and it was often unclear which materials students were expected to read and prepare before class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Managing Climate Security Crisis. The course covers a highly relevant and interesting topic that differs from many traditional political science courses. It also provides a valuable introduction to military planning and security perspectives. The professor, Michael, was very knowledgeable and engaging, which made the course particularly rewarding.

questions.answer: Nothing

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Eating out was less expensive than I had expected. There were many affordable cafés, restaurants, and student dining options, making it possible to eat out regularly without spending too much.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not make much use of the non-academic opportunities available, so my rating should not be seen as a reflection of the institution's offerings. There appeared to be a variety of activities, but I was not personally involved in them.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The university offered a range of cultural, athletic, and social activities for students. However, I did not participate in many of them myself, so I do not feel I am the best person to evaluate the range or quality of these activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would highly recommend travelling around France during the exchange period. Paris is very well connected by train, making it easy to visit other parts of the country. There are many great destinations that can be reached on day trips, allowing students to experience different regions, cultures, and landscapes without spending too much time or money.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend making the most of both Paris and the rest of France. Paris has an incredible amount to offer in terms of culture, history, food, and city life, while the excellent train network makes it easy to explore other regions of the country during weekends and holidays.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy to adjust to the local culture. In many ways, life in France felt similar to Denmark, and most people, especially students and younger people, spoke English, which made everyday life and social interactions much easier.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Learning some French is highly recommended. It can be difficult to get to know local students if you do not speak French, as many social interactions take place in French.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language barrier was the most challenging cultural difference. Speaking French is often important for everyday interactions and for fully integrating into local student life.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: What I appreciated most was the food, the culture, and the beauty of the city. The abundance of museums, historic landmarks, and stunning architecture made Paris an incredible place to live and explore.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Be patient with registration and administration.
2. Learn some French before arriving.
3. Ask for help when you need it, the staff are usually very supportive.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do not let the administrative challenges discourage you. Things often work out in the end, and the experience of living in Paris is well worth it. Make the most of the city, travel around France, and try to learn some French before arriving.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of my exchange experience was meeting new people and making friends from Denmark, France, and many other countries. The international community was one of the highlights of my stay.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was probably managing my budget. Living in Paris can be expensive, especially because there are so many things to see, do, and experience. However, I do not think financial concerns should discourage anyone from going on exchange. It is possible to live relatively affordably, and there are many inexpensive or free activities in the city. Some of my favorite moments were actually the simplest ones, such as sitting by the Seine with a croissant and a good book.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
